chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The hand of the thief is not cut off until his theft reaches one-quarter of a dinar, and Ali (peace be upon him) had cut [the hand] for an egg of iron.

Ali (peace be upon him) said, and Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut, so he said: For an egg of iron. I said: And what is its price? He said: One-quarter of a dinar.

key_terms.بَيْضَةِ حَدِيدٍ: Egg of iron (a specific object/measure used to illustrate the value threshold)
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: One-quarter of a dinar (a specific monetary value used as a threshold)
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: Is cut (referring to the amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for cutting the thief's hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the nisab (minimum value) for hadd al-sariqa, establishing one-quarter of a dinar as the threshold while resolving apparent contradictions through the principle of talfiq (synthesis) or contextual application by Imam al-Sadiq. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the general statutory limit and specific precedents, such as the 'egg of iron,' demonstrating how jurists reconcile textual evidence with practical legal rulings in Shia fiqh. The reference to Ali ibn Abi Hamzah or Imam Ali himself underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition in determining material worth for corporal punishments.
